doc.title: Jerry Bergonzi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 7, 2022

title: The four elements and Gary Smulyan's four
summary: Bergonzi explains earth, fire, water and air as aspects of music and compares them with Gary Smulyan's think, hear, feel, execute.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I was — I saw another interview with you which I was happy that I landed on, and you were talking about the four elements and it reminded me that I had this interesting interview with Gary Smulyan. And he had four elements of music but they were different from yours. So before I talk about his, would you mind telling me that again?

Sure. In astrology and metaphysics there’s four elements. There’s earth, fire, water, and air. And there’s three fire signs, there’s three air signs, there’s three water signs and three earth signs in the twelve signs of the zodiac. Fire of course is energy. It could be scorched earth energy or it could be warm fire or a cool fire you know. It could be the fire of intuition. It could be the fire of — and air is intellect. And whatever frequency your mind is at I mean it could be higher mind, lower mind, you know from thinking about you know eating all day is different than thinking of how to — not that that’s bad because you know nutrition is important, but how to invent a cure for cancer, you know, things like that. So water is emotion. And the higher is inspiration. That’s — you know you’re getting inspired and it comes from the emotional body, where intellect is intuition. That’s the higher aspect of the mental body. And earth is groove. It’s time. It’s how to play your instrument. It’s like you know I’ve got to bring these inspiration and intuition down and make it on this planet earth. That’s earth. Earth signs. So everybody has all four to some degree or another people might have a preponderance of a certain quality. So they’re just
words but sometimes it gives you what you hear and you say yeah, this guy really has a lot of air or this guy is so emotional but maybe could use a little bit of this or that, whatever.
When you listen to yourself does it occur to you that you could use a little more or a little less of something?

Yeah. Sometimes I’m thinking like yeah it’s like I was burning too hot. You know too much fire in that. I’m just going to learn the less I play the better I like it, the more I like it. You know things like that or I think yeah there’s something missing here. I’ll think like that. I won’t necessarily — yeah I need more air, I need more water. No, it’s more in a musical terms.
I see. Gary Smulyan said his four were: what you can think, what you can hear, what you can feel and what you can execute.
Yes it does indeed. It’s just a different way of putting it.
Hear is water. What you — say the other ones again?
Yeah and what you can hear.
What you can feel, which I guess would be like —
Yeah. Well I’m glad we solved that.
